title: Leticia Juarez Begins UISD Tenure Focused on Finances and Schools
excerpt: Newly elected United ISD trustee Leticia “Letty” Juarez took office this month with a clear first job: get a full picture of the district's finances and work toward long-term stability.
content:
Newly elected United ISD trustee Leticia “Letty” Juarez took office this month with a clear first job: get a complete understanding of the district’s financial situation and work toward restoring long-term financial stability.

Juarez, a longtime community advocate and former educator, was sworn in Wednesday, November 11, during a special-called meeting at the Bill Johnson Student Activity Center. Judge Eduardo “Wayo” Davila Jr. administered the oath as her family stood beside her.

She defeated Stephanie Maegan Valdez in the November 3 election, 4,365 votes to 2,806, and succeeds Javier Montemayor Jr., who did not seek re-election after 16 years as a UISD trustee.

She joins the board as the district continues to deal with financial difficulties, declining enrollment, school closures and concerns about employee compensation and benefits.

A former chief accountant and retired teacher, Juarez said she understands responsible financial management while making sure campuses have the resources and personnel students need. She wants to look for ways to cut administrative costs and improve efficiency before considering more school closures or cuts that directly affect campuses.

Supporting teachers and campus staff is another priority: reducing unnecessary paperwork, addressing staffing needs and making sure employees have the tools and support they need.

She also aims to strengthen transparency, accountability and community involvement, asking of every spending decision: “How does this benefit our students and their education?” “Every dollar we spend should be thoughtfully and responsibly used to support our students,” she said.

“After three years attending board meetings and advocating for our students, teachers and community, I am ready to bring that experience and commitment to the board,” Juarez said.
